theory_html:
A. Love, like and hate
A. Yêu, thích và ghét

From strongest to weakest: love (++), like (+), don’t like (–), hate (– –). I love my family. I hate spiders.

Từ mạnh đến yếu: yêu, thích, không thích, ghét.

B. Happy, sad and tired
B. Vui, buồn và mệt

  • happy, sad, angry, upset, cold, hot, thirsty, hungry, well, ill, tired, surprised – vui, buồn, giận, buồn bực, lạnh, nóng, khát, đói, khỏe, ốm, mệt, ngạc nhiên

happy about your news; happy for you (you did well).

happy about (vui về) tin của bạn; happy for (mừng cho) bạn.

C. Prefer, hope and want
C. Thích hơn, hy vọng, muốn

I prefer coffee to tea. I hope to do well / I hope (that) my friend does well. I want a new car / to buy a car / my mother to buy a car. Not I want that you help me.

prefer A to B (thích A hơn B); hope to do / hope (that)…; want sth / to do / sb to do. Không nói want that….

D. Expressions
D. Cách nói

Do you like football? – Yes, I really like it. / No, I don’t like it very much. (not I very like / I like very much football). How’s your grandfather? – He’s very well. – She’s a bit tired.

Bạn thích bóng đá không? – Có, rất thích. / Không thích lắm. Không nói I very like.

items.def_en: To like someone or something very much.
items.def_vi: Rất thích, yêu ai hoặc cái gì.
items.grammar_vi: Love (verb) = yêu, rất thích. Grammar: love + danh từ/V-ing/to V: I love swimming. Collocations / chunks: love my family (yêu gia đình). Word family: lovely (adj.).

example.en: I love my family and my best friend.
example.vi: Tôi yêu gia đình và người bạn thân nhất.

items.def_en: To enjoy something or think someone or something is nice.
items.def_vi: Thấy ai hay cái gì dễ chịu, thích.
items.grammar_vi: Like (verb) = thích. Grammar: like + V-ing: I like swimming; really like. Common mistakes: không nói I very like hay I like very much football.

items.def_en: To not enjoy or not want something.
items.grammar_vi: Don’t like (verb phrase) = không thích. Grammar: don’t like … very much (không thích lắm). Collocations / chunks: I don’t like horror films..

items.def_en: To dislike someone or something very much.
items.grammar_vi: Hate (verb) = ghét. Grammar: hate + danh từ/V-ing: I hate getting up early. Word family: hatred (n.).
Happy (adjective) = vui, hạnh phúc. Grammar: happy about sth (vui về điều gì), happy for sb (mừng cho ai). Common mistakes: không nói happy for your news.

example.en: I am very happy about your news.
example.vi: Tôi rất vui về tin của bạn.

example.en: She felt sad when her friend went away.
example.vi: Cô ấy thấy buồn khi bạn đi xa.

items.def_en: Having a strong feeling about something bad that someone has done.
items.def_vi: Có cảm xúc mạnh vì việc xấu ai đó làm.
items.grammar_vi: Angry (adjective) = giận. Grammar: angry with sb (giận ai), angry about sth (giận về việc gì). Word family: anger (n.).

example.en: My dad was angry because I came home late.

items.def_en: Unhappy or worried because something bad has happened.
items.def_vi: Buồn hoặc lo vì chuyện không hay.
items.grammar_vi: Upset (adjective) = buồn bực, khó chịu. Grammar: trọng âm âm tiết 2 /ʌpˈset/; upset about sth. Collocations / chunks: very upset (rất buồn).

example.en: She was upset because she failed her exam.
example.vi: Cô ấy buồn bực vì trượt kỳ thi.

items.def_en: Feeling that your body has a low temperature.
items.grammar_vi: Cold (adjective) = lạnh. Grammar: người dùng be cold (không nói have cold). Common mistakes: a cold (n.) = cảm lạnh.

example.en: Put on a coat if you are cold.
example.vi: Mặc áo khoác vào nếu bạn thấy lạnh.

items.def_en: Feeling that your body has a high temperature.

example.vi: Mở cửa sổ đi, tôi nóng quá.

example.en: I’m thirsty – can I have a glass of water?
example.vi: Tôi khát – cho tôi cốc nước nhé?

items.def_en: Feeling that you need to rest or sleep.
items.def_vi: Cảm thấy cần nghỉ hoặc ngủ.
items.grammar_vi: Tired (adjective) = mệt. Grammar: a bit / a little tired (hơi mệt); tired of sth (chán việc gì). Collocations / chunks: very tired (rất mệt).

example.en: B She’s a bit / a little tired.

items.def_en: Feeling that something unexpected has happened.
items.def_vi: Cảm thấy có điều bất ngờ xảy ra.
items.grammar_vi: Surprised (adjective) = ngạc nhiên. Grammar: surprised to see/hear; surprised at/by sth. Word family: surprise (n.), surprising (adj.).

example.en: I was very surprised to see him here.
example.vi: Tôi rất ngạc nhiên khi gặp anh ấy ở đây.

items.def_en: To like one thing more than another.
items.def_vi: Thích cái này hơn cái kia.
items.grammar_vi: Prefer (verb) = thích hơn. Grammar: prefer A to B; quá khứ preferred (gấp đôi r); trọng âm âm 2. Common mistakes: không nói prefer A than B.

items.def_en: To want something to happen and think that it is possible.
items.def_vi: Mong điều gì xảy ra và tin là có thể.
items.grammar_vi: Hope (verb) = hy vọng. Grammar: hope to do sth; hope (that) + mệnh đề. Collocations / chunks: I hope so (mong là vậy).

example.en: I hope to do well in my exam.
example.vi: Tôi hy vọng làm bài thi tốt.

items.def_en: To wish to have or do something.
items.grammar_vi: Want (verb) = muốn. Grammar: want sth / to do sth / sb to do sth. Common mistakes: không nói I want that you help me.

example.vi: Tôi muốn một chiếc ô tô mới.

items.def_en: Used to ask about another person or thing.
items.def_vi: Dùng để hỏi về người hay vật khác.
items.grammar_vi: How about (phrase) = còn … thì sao?. Grammar: how about + danh từ/V-ing. Collocations / chunks: How about you? (còn bạn?). Note: cũng dùng để gợi ý: How about a coffee?.
A bit (phrase) = hơi, một chút. Grammar: a bit + tính từ: a bit tired; thân mật hơn a little. Collocations / chunks: a bit cold (hơi lạnh).

example.en: B She’s a bit / a little tired.
